record.paper_title: Algorithmic Semi-algebraic Geometry and Topology -- Recent Progress and Open Problems
record.context_brief: All Betti numbers in single-exponential time
record.original_question: Let S be a semi-algebraic subset of R^k described by s polynomials of degree at most d. The Betti numbers b_i(S) are the dimensions of the homology or cohomology groups of S, equivalently the numbers of independent i-dimensional holes in the relevant dimensions. Does there exist an algorithm whose running time is single exponential in k for computing all Betti numbers of S? Known single-exponential algorithms compute only b_0(S), ..., b_ell(S) when ell is fixed in advance.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^k$ be a semi-algebraic set described by a Boolean combination of sign conditions on $s$ polynomials in $\mathbb{R}[X_1,\dots,X_k]$, each of degree at most $d$. For each integer $i \ge 0$, let $b_i(S) = \dim_{\mathbb{Q}} H_i(S;\mathbb{Q})$ be the $i$-th Betti number of $S$ (the dimension of its $i$-th singular homology group with rational coefficients); equivalently, $b_i(S)$ counts the number of independent $i$-dimensional holes of $S$.

Does there exist an algorithm that, given such a description of $S$, computes all the Betti numbers $b_0(S), b_1(S), \dots, b_k(S)$ in time bounded by $(sd)^{k^{O(1)}}$ (i.e., singly exponential in $k$)?

Remark on the state of knowledge: algorithms of complexity singly exponential in $k$ are known for computing $b_0(S),\dots,b_\ell(S)$ when $\ell$ is fixed in advance, as well as for the Euler–Poincaré characteristic; the question asks whether such a complexity can be achieved for all Betti numbers simultaneously.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem remains open. Singly exponential algorithms are known for the Euler–Poincaré characteristic, for $b_0$ and $b_1$, and more generally for the first $\ell+1$ Betti numbers with complexity $(sd)^{k^{O(\ell)}}$ when $\ell$ is fixed (Basu and collaborators). Computing all Betti numbers (especially middle ones) in single exponential time in $k$ is still considered a major open question in algorithmic real algebraic geometry; obstacles include the lack of a singly exponential triangulation algorithm.
